answer: A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, thus it pays the jetty fee twice and still divides one payout. Because the relic ledger attributes every share, the sonnet audit shows the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 80% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. The deposit is 7 dollars a seat. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
